prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1149; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for a left-turn collision at an intersection. Insured states the other vehicle came through on the opposing green. Claimant reports a knee injury and is handling the matter directly with no attorney on record. Photos requested from both parties.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant describes striking the knee on the dashboard during impact and reports ongoing pain when bending. Claimant confirmed no representation and asked for the claim process in writing. Sent the standard claimant information packet.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report. Officer notes the insured's vehicle was turning left across the path of oncoming traffic. Witness statement obtained from a pedestrian at the corner. Liability appears to lean toward the insured, pending review of traffic signal timing data.

Entry 4: Received medical documentation from the claimant's treating clinic. Diagnosis indicates a soft tissue injury to the knee with follow-up scheduled. Claimant still unrepresented. Explained that the claimant may consult an attorney at any time and that the company will continue to communicate directly while the file is open.

Entry 5: Requested the claimant's recorded statement regarding the sequence of events and the onset of knee symptoms. Claimant agreed to provide it next week. Set reserve review for injury and property damage. File remains open pending medical updates and the liability determination.
